mainTopic: Proper conduct of judges and leaders (דברים 1:17), a court summons with three, three experts for fines, and why a מוציא שם רע case needs twenty-three
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story: רב refuses to judge his host, who had done him favors, and sends רב כהנא, who warns the host that his tie to רב will not help him. The גמרא then explains דברים 1:17 phrase by phrase. A small-money case must not be pushed behind a big one. A judge must not hold back his opinion out of fear. Crooked judges make הקב״ה return the money to its owners. On whether משה was punished for saying 'bring the hard case to me,' רב נחמן בר יצחק points out that the פסוק says 'I will hear it,' and a ברייתא explains that the law of inheritance came through בנות צלפחד because they earned it. Two pairs of פסוקים teach that the people must respect the judge while the judge carries the people like a nurse carries a baby, and that a generation has one leader. Turning back to הלכה, the גמרא shows that 'זימון with three' means a court summons, which must come in the name of all three judges except on the set court day. It proves that דיני קנסות need three expert judges, so one expert is not enough. Finally, עולא and רבא give two explanations of why the חכמים require twenty-three judges for a מוציא שם רע case.

steps.title: רב refuses to judge his host and sends רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: רב tells his host that he cannot judge his case and sends רב כהנא to judge it instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I am disqualified from judging your case.' רב said to רב כהנא: 'Go out and judge it.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a story: רב's host brought a case to רב, and רב says he cannot be the judge. He hands the case over to his student רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The host had done favors for רב, so רב worries he might lean toward him. Rather than risk being unfair, רב removes himself completely and lets someone else judge.

keyTerms.meaning: I am disqualified (not allowed to act as judge)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows in real life how seriously חכמים took even a small chance of being biased.

phrases.english: I am disqualified from judging for you.
phrases.notes: רב is talking to his host, the man he was staying with, who had done things for him.

phrases.english: Rav said to Rav Kahana:
Go out and judge it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story that began before this section, about רב and his host.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge who has received favors from someone should step away from judging that person's case.

steps.title: רב כהנא puts the haughty host in his place
steps.stepSummary: The host acts proud because he is close to רב, and רב כהנא warns him that this connection will not help him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא saw that the host was acting arrogantly about it. He said to him: 'If you will listen, listen. And if not, I will take רב out of your ear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The host thinks his friendship with רב will get him a better result. רב כהנא tells him clearly that it won't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after רב stepped away, the host tried to use his closeness to רב. רב כהנא's sharp warning shows that a judge must not let anyone's connections affect the case.
steps.whatToRemember: רב stepped away because of his own possible bias, and רב כהנא made sure the host's connection to רב would not affect the ruling.

phrases.english: He saw that he was acting haughtily about it.
phrases.notes: רב כהנא is the one who sees, and the host is the one acting proud because of his tie to רב.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If you will listen, listen;
and if not,
I will take Rav out of your ear.
phrases.notes: Basically: I'll make you stop thinking רב will save you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes the story of רב's host.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A litigant's personal connections must have no effect on how the case is judged.

steps.title: A small case must be as dear as a big case
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains the פסוק 'hear the small and the great alike': a case about a פרוטה must be as important to the judge as a case about a hundred מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You shall hear the small and the great alike.' ריש לקיש says: A case about one פרוטה should be as dear to you as a case about a hundred מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the next words of the פסוק. ריש לקיש says 'small' and 'great' means small and large amounts of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think 'small and great' means poor and rich people. ריש לקיש reads it as small and large sums: the size of the amount must not change how much the judge cares about the case.

phrases.english: "You shall hear the small and the great alike."
phrases.notes: דברים 1:17

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא חָבִיב עָלֶיךָ דִּין שֶׁל פְּרוּטָה
phrases.english: That a case of one peruta should be as dear to you
as a case of one hundred maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story, the גמרא returns to explaining the words of דברים 1:17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small-money case must be treated as just as important as a large-money case.

steps.title: What practical rule does this teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ריש לקיש's teaching changes in practice, and rejects the idea that it means judging small cases carefully, since that is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what practical law? If you say it means to look into the case carefully and decide it, that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what ריש לקיש is actually teaching us. It tries one answer and throws it out because everyone already knows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of course a judge must study and decide a small case properly; a judge cannot rule carelessly just because the amount is small. So ריש לקיש must be teaching something more, and the גמרא is setting up the real answer in the next step.

phrases.english: For what practical law?
If you say: to look into it carefully and decide it,
that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what ריש לקיש's teaching means in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference does ריש לקיש's teaching make?

steps.title: It is about which case is heard first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש means a small case cannot be pushed aside so that a bigger case is heard first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about giving it precedence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning of ריש לקיש: it is about the order of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the small case came first, the judge may not delay it just because a larger case is waiting. This is a real rule that we would not have known without the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: to put it first / give it precedence

steps.whatToRemember: 'Small and great alike' means a small-money case is not pushed behind a big-money case in the order of hearing.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to give it precedence.
phrases.notes: If the small case came first, it gets heard first. It doesn't wait for the bigger one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש's teaching is about the order of cases: a small case may not be delayed in favor of a big one.

steps.title: Do not hold back your opinion out of fear
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנן explains 'do not be afraid of any man': a judge must not keep his words in because of anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Do not be afraid of any man.' רבי חנן says: Do not hold in your words because of any person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the פסוק. רבי חנן says a judge must say his honest opinion even if someone powerful is involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Fear' here means keeping quiet out of fear. The judge must not swallow his true opinion because a litigant or someone else might frighten him.

keyTerms.meaning: do not hold in (literally: do not bring in)

phrases.english: "You shall not be afraid of any man."
Rabbi Chanan says:
Do not hold back your words because of any person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase in דברים 1:17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge must state his honest opinion and not hold it back out of fear of anyone.

steps.title: Crooked judges make ה׳ fix their damage
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains 'for the judgment is God's': הקב״ה complains that wicked judges not only take money unfairly but make Him return it to its owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For the judgment is God's.' רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says: הקב״ה said: It is not enough for the wicked that they take money from one person and give it to another unfairly, but they also trouble Me to return the money to its owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the פסוק. Since judgment really belongs to ה׳, when judges rule wrongly, ה׳ Himself steps in to set things right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unfair judges do two wrongs: they steal from one side, and they force ה׳ to fix it. This shows how serious a false ruling is, since it is a wrong done in ה׳'s own area.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not enough for them
not according to the law; unfairly

phrases.english: "For the judgment is God's."
Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina says:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
It is not enough for the wicked

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנּוֹטְלִין מִזֶּה מָמוֹן וְנוֹתְנִים לָזֶה שֶׁלֹּא כַּדִּין,
phrases.english: that they take money from this one and give it to that one unlawfully,
but they also trouble Me
to return the money to its owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because judgment is ה׳'s, a false ruling forces ה׳ to return the money to its rightful owner.

steps.title: משה was punished for 'bring the hard case to me'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא (or רבי יאשיה) says משה was punished for saying 'the hard case, bring it to me,' and the proof is that later he could not answer the daughters of צלפחד himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the matter that is too hard for you.' רבי חנינא, and some say רבי יאשיה, says: For this matter משה was punished, as it says: 'And משה brought their case before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last part of the פסוק, where משה says hard cases should be brought to him. This אמורא says משה was punished for sounding too sure of himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה said 'bring it to me,' as if he would always know the answer. Measure for measure, when the daughters of צלפחד came with their case, he did not know the law and had to bring it before ה׳.

phrases.english: "And the matter that is too hard for you."
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on: 'bring it to me and I will hear it.' That is the part being discussed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina, and some say Rabbi Yoshiya, says:
For this matter Moshe was punished,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיַּקְרֵב מֹשֶׁה אֶת מִשְׁפָּטָן לִפְנֵי ה׳״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: "And Moshe brought their case before the Lord."
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:5, the case of the daughters of צלפחד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next words of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה's statement 'bring it to me' was too confident, and he was punished by not knowing the law of צלפחד's daughters.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: משה only said 'I will hear it'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges the idea that משה was boastful: the פסוק says 'I will hear it,' not 'I will tell you,' meaning 'if I know, I know, and if not, I will go and learn.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק objects: Is it written 'and I will tell you'? It is written 'and I will hear it'! Meaning: if I have learned it, I have learned it; and if not, I will go and learn it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק argues against the previous step. He points to the exact word משה used to show that משה was not being proud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I will tell you' would sound like משה promised to always have the answer. But 'I will hear it' only means משה would listen to the case, and if he did not know the law, he would go and learn it, which is exactly what he did with צלפחד's daughters.

keyTerms.meaning: and I will tell you (make you hear)
I have learned / I will learn

steps.whatToRemember: One opinion says משה was punished for 'bring it to me.' רב נחמן בר יצחק disagrees: 'I will hear it' is humble, meaning 'if I don't know, I'll go learn.'
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two words: 'וְאַשְׁמִיעֲכֶם' (I will tell you) is NOT in the פסוק. The פסוק says 'וּשְׁמַעְתִּיו' (I will hear it), and that is the whole point of the challenge.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak objects to this:
Is it written "and I will tell you"?
"And I will hear it" is written!
If I have learned it, I have learned it;
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן explaining what משה meant by 'I will hear it.'

phrases.english: and if not, I will go and learn it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 8's claim that משה was punished.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of רבי חנינא / רבי יאשיה that משה was punished for 'bring it to me.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording of the פסוק is 'I will hear it,' not 'I will tell you,' so משה never claimed to know every answer; he only said he would listen and, if needed, go and learn.

steps.title: The inheritance law came through the daughters because they earned it
steps.stepSummary: The law of inheritance could have come directly through משה. It came through בנות צלפחד because they earned the honor. In the same way, the law of the מקושש came through him because he sinned. Good is brought about through good people, and bad through guilty people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, as a ברייתא teaches: the section about inheritances should have been written through משה רבינו, but the daughters of צלפחד earned it, so it was written through them. The section about the wood-gatherer should have been written through משה רבינו, but the wood-gatherer became guilty, so it was written through him. This teaches you that bad things are brought about through a guilty person, and good things through a good person.
steps.whatsHappening: In step 9, רב נחמן בר יצחק said משה was not boastful. That leaves a question: why did the inheritance law come through the daughters? Here the גמרא gives a new reason. They earned the honor, so it was not a punishment for משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said משה was punished because he could not answer the daughters himself. After step 9 rejected that idea, the גמרא needs another explanation, and it brings one from a ברייתא. The general rule is that ה׳ sends good things through people who deserve them, and harsh things through people who deserve those.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who gathered wood on שבת
Bring about, cause to come through someone

steps.whatToRemember: Good things come through good people, and bad things come through guilty people.

phrases.english: Rather, as it was taught:
phrases.notes: Since step 9 said משה wasn't boastful, the גמרא now gives a different reason the law came through the daughters.

phrases.english: The section about inheritances was fit
to be written through משה our teacher,
but the daughters of צלפחד earned it
and it was written through them.
The section about the wood-gatherer was fit
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:32

phrases.english: to be written through משה our teacher,
but the wood-gatherer became guilty
and it was written through him.

phrases.aramaic: לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁמְגַלְגְּלִין חוֹבָה עַל יְדֵי חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: To teach you that bad things are brought about through a guilty person,
and good things through a good person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reason for the daughters' law after step 9 rejected the 'punishment' reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the same event
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The law came through the daughters as a punishment for משה
steps.terutzMaskana: It came through them because they earned the honor

steps.title: Two verses: commanding the judges versus commanding everyone
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק says משה commanded the judges. A nearby פסוק says he commanded the whole people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'And I commanded your judges at that time.' And it is written: 'And I commanded you at that time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out two פסוקים that seem to clash: who did משה command, the judges or everyone? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the same words, 'at that time.' One is addressed to the judges and the other to the people. The גמרא wants to know why there are two separate commands.

phrases.english: It is written: 'And I commanded your judges at that time,'
phrases.notes: דברים 1:16

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And I commanded you at that time.'
phrases.notes: דברים 1:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about פסוקים on judges
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two similar commands go to different audiences, so why are both needed?

steps.title: The people must respect the judge, and the judge must bear with the people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי שמלאי says each פסוק is a separate warning. The community must be in awe of the judge, and the judge must patiently put up with the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי שמלאי: it is a warning to the community to be in awe of the judge, and a warning to the judge to bear with the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step. Each פסוק gives its own warning to a different group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither פסוק is extra. The one to the people tells them to respect judges. The one to the judges tells them to carry the people's burden with patience.

keyTerms.meaning: That he should bear, put up with

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי:
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי שמלאי:
A warning to the community
that the awe of the judge should be upon them,
and a warning to the judge
that he should bear with the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clash between the two פסוקים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק speaks to a different audience
steps.terutzMaskana: The people must respect the judge, and the judge must bear with the people

steps.title: How far must the judge bear with the people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much a judge must put up with.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question about the judge's duty. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the judge must bear with the community but did not say how much. The question asks for the limit.

phrases.english: Up to how much?
phrases.notes: He means: how far must the judge go in bearing with the people?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the judge's duty from step 12 goes
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much the judge must bear with the community

steps.title: Like a nurse carrying a nursing baby
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנן (some say רבי שבתאי) answers with a פסוק: the judge must carry the people the way a nurse carries a nursing baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנן, and some say רבי שבתאי, said: 'As a nurse carries the nursing baby.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers how far the judge must go. He must carry the people with the gentle, full care that a baby needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby needs constant patience and care. The judge's patience must reach that level, which is a very high standard.

keyTerms.meaning: The nurse, the one who raises a child

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנָן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי שַׁבְּתַאי:
phrases.english: רבי חנן said, and some say רבי שבתאי:
'As a nurse carries the nursing baby.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:12

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנָן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי שַׁבְּתַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The judge must bear with the people like a nurse carrying a baby

steps.title: Two verses: 'you will go' versus 'you will bring'
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק tells יהושע 'you will go' with the people. Another tells him 'you will bring' the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'For you will go,' and it is written: 'For you will bring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out another pair of פסוקים that do not match. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Go' sounds like יהושע travels alongside the people. 'Bring' sounds like he leads them himself. The גמרא wants to know which one is true.

phrases.english: It is written: 'For you will go,'
phrases.notes: דברים 31:7

phrases.english: and it is written: 'For you will bring.'
phrases.notes: דברים 31:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new pair of clashing פסוקים, built the same way as step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Go' and 'bring' describe two different kinds of leadership

steps.title: One leader for a generation, not two
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the two פסוקים. משה told יהושע to lead together with the elders. הקב״ה told him to lead alone and firmly, because a generation has one leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: משה told יהושע, 'You and the elders of the generation will be with them.' הקב״ה told him, 'Take a stick and hit them on their heads.' One leader for a generation, not two leaders for a generation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the clash. Each פסוק comes from a different speaker: one is from משה and the other is from הקב״ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Go' is משה's advice to share leadership with the elders. 'Bring' is הקב״ה's command that יהושע lead by himself with authority. The lesson is that a generation needs one clear leader.
steps.whatToRemember: A generation has one leader, not two.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
משה said to יהושע:
You and the elders of the generation will be with them.
phrases.notes: This matches 'you will go': going along together with the people and the elders.

phrases.english: הקב״ה said to him:
Take a stick and hit them on their heads.
phrases.notes: This matches 'you will bring': you yourself lead them, with firm authority.

phrases.english: One leader for a generation,
and not two leaders for a generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clash in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different speakers: משה's advice versus הקב״ה's command
steps.terutzMaskana: A generation must have one leader

steps.title: A ברייתא: זימון is with three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says זימון is done with three people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: זימון is with three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to halachic topics. It quotes a short ברייתא that it will now examine, so this line sets up the next questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the word זימון without explaining it. That unclear word is what the גמרא is about to discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'invitation'; its exact meaning here is about to be discussed

phrases.english: It was taught: זימון is with three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the teachings of אגדה and returns to הלכה

steps.title: What does זימון mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by the word זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is זימון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word means. This opens the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'with three' depends on what זימון means, so the גמרא has to define the word first.

phrases.english: What is זימון?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of זימון in the ברייתא

steps.title: It cannot simply mean ברכת זימון
steps.stepSummary: If זימון meant ברכת זימון, why would another ברייתא list 'זימון and ברכת זימון' as two items?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means ברכת זימון, but it was taught: 'זימון and ברכת זימון are with three'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the obvious answer, ברכת זימון, the invitation to bentch together. It then attacks that answer right away using another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That other ברייתא names זימון and ברכת זימון side by side. Listing them separately suggests they are two different things, so זימון must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: The invitation to bentch together after a meal

phrases.english: If you say it means ברכת זימון,
but it was taught: 'זימון and ברכת זימון are with three'!
phrases.notes: Naming both together suggests they are two different things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to step 18 and attacks it
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that זימון means ברכת זימון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא lists them separately, so they must be different things

steps.title: The idea that the ברייתא is explaining itself is rejected
steps.stepSummary: Someone might read the second ברייתא as explaining itself: 'זימון, meaning ברכת זימון.' The גמרא rejects this with a third ברייתא that says 'with three' about each one separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is explaining itself, 'What is זימון? ברכת זימון,' but it was taught: 'זימון is with three, ברכת זימון is with three'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines a defense: the ברייתא with 'זימון and ברכת זימון' is just explaining one term with the other. Then it knocks that defense down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third ברייתא says 'with three' twice, once for each term. This shows clearly that they are two separate items, so זימון still cannot mean ברכת זימון. The next step gives the real meaning.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא has concluded what זימון means. So far it has only shown that זימון is NOT ברכת זימון. The next step gives the real meaning.

phrases.english: And if you say it is explaining itself:
phrases.notes: Maybe the 'and' in 'זימון and ברכת זימון' really means 'that is.'

phrases.english: What is זימון? ברכת זימון.
But it was taught: 'זימון is with three,'
'ברכת זימון is with three'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Imagines a defense against step 19 and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the ברייתא is explaining one term with the other
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A third ברייתא says 'with three' about each term separately, so they are two different things

steps.title: זימון means a court summons
steps.stepSummary: Since זימון cannot mean ברכת זימון, the גמרא explains that it means summoning someone to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is זימון? It means summoning a person to court for judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers the question from step 18. 'זימון with three' means a court summons, not the blessing after a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 19-20 showed that זימון and ברכת זימון are two separate things. So זימון needs a different meaning, and the גמרא gives one: an official call to come to בית דין. That is why the ברייתא says it needs three, the number of judges on a court.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the זימון said before ברכת המזון. Here the word means calling someone to court.

phrases.english: Rather, what is zimmun?
Summoning to judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real meaning of זימון after the ברכת זימון reading was ruled out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word זימון means in the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means a summons to court

steps.title: רבא: a summons must come in the name of all three judges
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a court messenger who summons someone in the name of only one judge has said nothing. He must speak in the name of all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבא said: when three judges are sitting, and the court's messenger goes and summons someone in the name of only one of them, he has said nothing. It only counts once he says it in the name of all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the new meaning of זימון with a ruling from רבא. A summons is only valid if it comes from the whole court of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that a summons really is a 'three-person' act. It must come from the whole court, so it makes sense that the ברייתא says זימון is done with three.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of all of them

phrases.english: Like that which Rava said:
These three judges who are sitting,
and the agent of the court went
and said it from the mouth of one,
phrases.notes: He means the messenger told the person, 'Judge so-and-so is calling you,' naming just one judge.

phrases.english: he has not said anything,
unless he said it in the name of all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation that זימון means a court summons.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that זימון in the ברייתא means a summons needing three
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling that a summons must be in the name of all three judges
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A summons given in the name of only one judge is not valid.

steps.title: On a court day, one judge's name is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא's rule applies only on a day that is not the set day for judgment. On the set day of judgment, a summons in one judge's name is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only when it is not the day of judgment. But on the day of judgment, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רבא's rule. On the set court day, a summons naming just one judge is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular day, a summons from one judge may not show that the whole court is behind it. On the court day, everyone knows the court is sitting, so naming one judge is understood as the whole court calling.

keyTerms.meaning: We have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: זימון by three means a court summons. It must come in the name of the whole court, except on the court day, when one judge's name is enough.

phrases.english: This applies when it is not the day of judgment,
but on the day of judgment,
we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבא's rule to days that are not the set day for judgment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the set day of judgment, a summons in the name of one judge is valid.

steps.title: How many judges are needed for fines?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about תשלומי כפל. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא sends a question to רב נחמן בר יעקב: how many judges are needed for דיני קנסות?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Double payment...' רב נחמן בר רב חסדא sent to רב נחמן בר יעקב: Let our teacher teach us, how many judges are needed for cases of fines?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about fines like paying double. It brings a question sent from one sage to another about how many judges such cases need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קנסות are payments that go beyond simply paying back the loss, like a thief paying double. The question is about the size of the court needed to rule on them.

keyTerms.meaning: Double payment that a thief pays
Cases of fines (payments beyond the actual damage)

phrases.english: Double payment, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the start of a line from the משנה. 'Etc.' means the rest of that line.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda sent
to Rav Naḥman bar Ya'akov:
Let our teacher instruct us,
cases of fines, by how many?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many judges are needed to judge cases of fines

steps.title: But the משנה already says three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders why he asked at all, since the משנה clearly says fines are judged by three.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his question? We learned in the משנה that it is by three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself. The משנה already gives the answer: three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great sage would not ask something that is stated plainly in the משנה. So the גמרא expects that his question must really be about something else.

phrases.english: What is he asking?
Didn't we learn: by three!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the question in step 24 was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already says three judges are needed, so there seems to be nothing to ask.

steps.title: The real question is about one expert judge
steps.stepSummary: His question was whether a single expert judge may rule on fines by himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was asking about a single expert judge: can he judge cases of fines or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real question. Three regular judges are needed, but can one expert judge do it alone?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An expert judge (מומחה) has extra authority. In money cases, one expert may sometimes judge alone. So the question was whether that also works for fines.

phrases.english: Rather, he is asking about a single expert,
does he judge cases of fines or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the question is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He was asking how many ordinary judges are needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was asking whether one expert judge is enough.

steps.title: You learned it: fines need three
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יעקב answers that the משנה already teaches that double payment and four or five payment need three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You learned it already: double payment and four-or-five payment are by three.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יעקב answers by pointing back to the משנה. He is setting up a proof that one expert is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the very משנה that says 'three.' The next steps will show how that word answers the question about a single expert.

keyTerms.meaning: Four or five times payment for stealing and slaughtering or selling a sheep or ox

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it,
double payment and payment of four and five
are by three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the real question from step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה requires three judges for fines. Steps 28-29 show that this means three experts, so a single expert is not enough.

steps.title: It cannot mean three regular judges
steps.stepSummary: What kind of three? Not three regular judges, because רב said even ten regular judges cannot judge fines.
steps.simpleTranslation: What three? If you say three regular judges, didn't your father's father say in the name of רב: even ten regular judges are not fit to judge fines!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יעקב asks what kind of 'three' the משנה means. He rules out regular, non-expert judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only experts can judge fines at all, as רב taught. So the משנה's 'three' must be talking about experts.

keyTerms.meaning: Regular judges who are not experts

phrases.english: What three?
If you say three lay judges,
didn't your father's father say in the name of Rav:
phrases.notes: That's the grandfather of רב נחמן בר רב חסדא, the one asking.

phrases.english: even ten, and they are lay judges,
are unfit for cases of fines!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the meaning of 'three' in the משנה he just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה's 'three' as three regular judges
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב taught that regular judges cannot judge fines at all, even ten of them.

steps.title: Three experts are needed, so one is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The משנה must mean experts, and it still says three, so a single expert cannot judge fines.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means experts, and it still says three.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the proof. Even with expert judges, the משנה requires three, so one expert alone cannot judge fines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'three' must mean experts, the number three is a real requirement for experts too. That answers the question: a יחיד מומחה may not judge דיני קנסות.
steps.whatToRemember: דיני קנסות need three expert judges. Regular judges cannot judge them at all, and a single expert is not enough.

phrases.english: Rather, experts, and it says three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from ruling out regular judges.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A single expert judge may not judge cases of fines. Three experts are required.

steps.title: The Rabbis: a defamer needs twenty-three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's view of the חכמים that a מוציא שם רע case is judged by twenty-three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: a מוציא שם רע is judged by twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. It is setting up a discussion of the מוציא שם רע case that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twenty-three is the size of a court for life-and-death cases. The coming discussion will explain why the חכמים require such a large court here.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who falsely claims his wife was unfaithful during אירוסין
Twenty-three, the court for capital cases

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
A defamer is by twenty-three.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, a מוציא שם רע case needs a court of twenty-three.

steps.title: Why does a possible capital side matter here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the חכמים: even if a מוציא שם רע case can sometimes be capital, why should that matter for a case that is only about money?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it contains capital law, so what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason the חכמים gave for using twenty-three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said a מוציא שם רע case needs twenty-three because it can involve דיני נפשות. The גמרא asks why that matters when this specific case has no capital side and is only about money. A money case normally needs only three judges.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband who claims his new wife was not a virgin, giving her a bad name
Capital cases, where a life is at stake
So what? What difference does it make?

phrases.english: And if it contains capital law,
phrases.notes: "It" is the מוציא שם רע case. The משנה's reason for twenty-three is that this kind of case can involve a capital side.

phrases.english: what of it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי יֵשׁ בּוֹ דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת, מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of the חכמים quoted in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' rule that a מוציא שם רע case needs twenty-three judges because it contains a capital side.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case being tried is only about money. A possible capital side that is not present here should not change the size of the court.

steps.title: עולא: The dispute is about worrying over rumors
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree about whether we worry about rumors. רבי מאיר says we do not, and the חכמים say we do.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: They disagree about whether we worry about rumors. רבי מאיר holds we do not worry about rumors, and the חכמים hold we do.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question by showing what the two sides of the משנה really disagree about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the case starts as a money case, the חכמים worry that the talk it creates could turn it into a capital case later. So they want a court of twenty-three from the start. רבי מאיר does not worry about this, so for him three judges are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: We worry about rumors or talk

phrases.english: Ulla said:
They disagree about whether we are concerned with rumors.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְלַעַז,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds: we are not concerned with rumors,
and the Rabbis hold: we are concerned with rumors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the underlying principle of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the case is only about money, the possible capital side should not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים worry that rumors could turn the case into a capital one, so they require twenty-three judges.

steps.title: רבא: The dispute is about honoring the first judges
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone agrees we do not worry about rumors. The real dispute is whether we must protect the honor of the first judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees we do not worry about rumors. Here they disagree about whether we worry about the honor of the first judges.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same question and rejects עולא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, rumors are not a concern for anyone. The disagreement is about respecting the judges who already started hearing the case. The חכמים care about that honor, and רבי מאיר does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The honor of the first judges

phrases.english: Rava said:
Everyone agrees we are not concerned with rumors,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּחוֹשְׁשִׁין לִכְבוֹדָן שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹנִים קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and here they disagree about whether we are concerned for the honor of the first judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לְלַעַז לָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 31 and rejects עולא's reasoning in step 32.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא's view: the dispute is about worrying over rumors.
steps.terutzMaskana: Nobody worries about rumors. The dispute is about the honor of the first judges.

steps.title: רבא describes the exact case
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the case. A court of twenty-three gathered for a capital case and broke up. Then the husband asked them to rule at least on the money part.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? A court of twenty-three gathered to judge a capital case and then broke up. The husband said to them: At least judge the money part for me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא fills in the case so we can see where the honor of the first judges comes in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the twenty-three judges already started on this case, the חכמים say the money part should also go back to them so they are not insulted. רבי מאיר says a regular court of three is enough for money matters.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

steps.whatToRemember: עולא: the dispute is about worrying over rumors. רבא: nobody worries about rumors, and the dispute is about honoring the twenty-three judges who already began the case.

phrases.english: And with what are we dealing here?
For example, where a court of twenty-three gathered
to judge capital law,
and they dispersed, and he said to them:
phrases.notes: "He" is the husband who brought the claim against his wife.

phrases.english: Judge for me at least the monetary law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case that רבא's explanation in step 33 refers to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It is unclear where the honor of the judges comes in for a money case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The twenty-three had already gathered for the capital side, so the חכמים want them to handle the money side too, to protect their honor.
